clue.text: "We get fed up about this government" (low-paid workers)

definitions.text: "We get fed up about this government"
definitions.meaning: a cryptic reading: we fretted ('sweated') over the party in power at the time, the Labour government
people toiling long hours for poor pay in harsh conditions

explanation.surface: A grumble from workers about the government of the day, with a bracketed gloss on who is speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: When this ran the government was Labour, so 'sweated Labour' can be read as 'we got anxious over this government'; the bracketed words give the ordinary meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard term for workforces exploited with long hours and poor pay in sweatshops.

clue.text: Wales gave unusual example of 1

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the letters take an odd order

explanation.surface: Wales provided an odd instance of exploited labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A drudge paid a pittance is a typical case of the exploited workers in 1 across.

clue.text: Notice antiquity of a proverb

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
age means antiquity, oldness

explanation.surface: Take note of how old a saying is.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a traditional saying expressing a common truth, a synonym of proverb.

clue.text: Isolates wavy lines between quarters

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit between the two compass quarters

parts.note: E and S, east and south, are compass quarters

indicators.note: wavy lines are not straight, so the letters wander out of order

explanation.surface: Wavy lines mark off sections on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wavy' turns LINES into NISLE, which goes between E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To enisle is a literary verb meaning to put on an island, hence to isolate.

clue.text: Go north in a car to get another

indicators.note: the go-north piece goes inside the car

parts.note: a Lada is a Russian make of car
taken as written
N is north

explanation.surface: Driving north in one vehicle to fetch a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another car, following on from 'a car'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagonda is a British luxury car marque, so it is another make of car.

clue.text: A little intelligence may be above the man in the street

definitions.meaning: a person of little intelligence, a fool

definitions.text: may be above the man in the street
definitions.meaning: a bird's brain flying overhead could be literally above a pedestrian

explanation.surface: A bit of smartness might set someone above ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdbrain is a silly person, and a bird's brain could literally be overhead.

clue.text: Cruel wound that's hard to heal

definitions.text: Cruel wound that's hard to heal

indicators.note: read as the past tense of wind, twisted, so the letters are twisted

explanation.surface: A nasty injury that will not mend easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like the noun injury but is the verb wind, twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is an open sore that is often slow and difficult to heal.

clue.text: Unfashionable run for sailors

parts.note: senior suggests old, and old-fashioned means unfashionable
a service is a regular run, as of buses or trains

explanation.surface: A dated route meant for seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Navy is called the Senior Service as the oldest of Britain's armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Navy is nicknamed the Senior Service, so its sailors are that service.

clue.text: Chairman tried to convert Greek ecclesiastic

indicators.note: converting changes something's form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A company head attempted to win over an Orthodox clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: An archimandrite is a senior abbot or cleric in the Greek Orthodox Church.

clue.text: Sassenachs, in short, mad about cutting out characters

parts.note: Sassenach is the Scots word for the English; English in short is ENG
raving means mad, wildly insane

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about the English, as a Scot might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link here, padding the surface; a Sassenach is what Scots call an English person.
explanation.definitionFit: Engraving is the craft of incising letters or designs into a hard surface, literally cutting out characters.

clue.text: One could be champion in a good car

definitions.text: One could be champion in a good car

indicators.note: the champion sits inside the car, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: RR, short for Rolls-Royce, the archetypal good car
an ace is a champion, a top performer

explanation.surface: A winning driver needs a decent motor.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a speed driver could become champion with a good enough car.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in motor sport could be crowned champion if their vehicle is good enough.

clue.text: Susie might have offspring

indicators.note: signals that the name's letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A woman called Susie may one day have children.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal and legal word for children or descendants.

clue.text: Flier got hind leg partially broken by accident

indicators.note: an accident throws things about, so these letters are jumbled
only part of the word broken is used, its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone hurt a hind leg in a mishap, perhaps a horse or dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' takes BR from 'broken'; jumble HINDLEG with BR to get the aviator's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lindbergh was the American aviator who made the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight in 1927.

clue.text: Colour is said to signify liquidity

indicators.note: tells us the words are spoken, sounding like the answer

parts.note: red is, a colour plus the word is

explanation.surface: A remark about what a certain colour means, as in red signalling debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready money in slang is 'the readies', cash on hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Readies is British slang for cash, money immediately available, which is what liquidity means in finance.

clue.text: Is one Gray the work of a Spanish saint?

definitions.text: the work of a Spanish saint

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
Dorian Gray is Oscar Wilde's character

explanation.surface: Is a book by one Gray really by a Spanish saint?
explanation.walkthrough: Saint Isidore of Seville was a scholar whose writings are described by this adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to Isidore of Seville, the Spanish saint and encyclopedist.

clue.text: A bad mouth may need this filling

definitions.text: A bad mouth may need this filling

parts.words: A bad mouth may need this filling
parts.note: reads like a remark about rude talk, but means a decayed set of teeth needing a dentist's filling material

explanation.surface: Someone foul-mouthed might need something to shut them up.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental amalgam is the mercury alloy traditionally used to fill cavities in decayed teeth.

clue.text: Engineer reading about another soldier

indicators.note: the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the army's engineers

explanation.surface: An army engineer reads up on a fellow soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' links to the engineer, a soldier too.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is a soldier, originally one who threw grenades, now a guardsman.

clue.text: Gray mood caused smart worker to leave 1 ac.

indicators.note: the worker leaves the smart word, so its letters are taken out

parts.note: elegant means smart, stylish
an ant is the crossword's standard worker
the Roman numeral one is I
ac. is an abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A gloomy atmosphere drove a stylish employee to quit, with a nod to another answer.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac.' looks like a cross-reference to 1 across but is read literally as I and AC; Gray wrote the famous Elegy in a Country Churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray's best-known poem is an elegy, and an elegiac mood is mournful and reflective.

clue.text: Something fishy leads to warning about air trip

indicators.note: the warning goes round the other piece

parts.note: cave, Latin for beware, is schoolboy slang for a warning

indicators.note: a trip makes one stumble, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: A dubious deal prompts a warning about a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' turns AIR into IAR, which goes inside CAVE. Caviare is an older spelling of caviar.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar is sturgeon roe, literally something from a fish.

clue.text: Can a bird have inspired the poet's quinquennial visit here?

parts.note: a tin is a can
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A whimsical question whether a bird inspired Wordsworth's return visit after five years.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's 'Lines written a few miles above Tintern Abbey' opens 'Five years have past', the quinquennial visit; 'here' points to the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbey in the Wye valley is the place the poet revisited after five years, so it is where the visit happened.

clue.text: Rent difficulty caused a storm

parts.note: rent as a past participle means torn
ado is fuss or difficulty

explanation.surface: Trouble over the rent led to a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm.

clue.text: Turn in vehicle insurance in Canada

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: the turn goes inside the insurance word

parts.note: cover is insurance protection
U as in a U-turn

explanation.surface: A U-turn made in a van, with talk of insurance, somewhere in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a major city on Canada's Pacific coast, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: Polish river's said to be preferable

indicators.note: the river's name is spoken, sounding like the answer

parts.note: the Nysa is a river in Poland

explanation.surface: A river in Poland is reputedly the better one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the verb shine; it is the nationality. The Nysa, said in a non-rhotic accent, matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nicer is more pleasant, and therefore preferable.

clue.text: Harsh sound of a politician

indicators.note: says the next word is heard rather than read, a soundalike

parts.note: a blare is a harsh loud noise

explanation.surface: A jibe that a politician's voice grates.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was Prime Minister when this appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair, the Labour leader and Prime Minister, is a well-known politician.

clue.text: Parton's characteristic blunders

definitions.meaning: Dolly Parton is famous for her large bust

explanation.surface: The trademark of the country singer, or her mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Boobs is slang both for breasts, Dolly Parton's trademark, and for foolish mistakes.

clue.text: To do in a number of Dalmatians could be prickly

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: 101, as in the film, is CI in Roman numerals
to act is to do

explanation.surface: Killing off a pack of spotted dogs would be a thorny business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To do in' tempts as the slang for kill; it is ACT followed by the containment signal. The number comes from the story 101 Dalmatians.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert succulents armed with spines are things that could be prickly to touch.

clue.text: One studies organic structure of western alliance in a fog

indicators.note: the alliance sits inside the fog

parts.note: a mist is a fog
NATO, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization

explanation.surface: Someone researches how a western military pact is lost in confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy is the science of bodily structure, so its specialist studies the structure of organisms.

clue.text: Royal spin in establishment with criminal class

parts.note: PR, public relations, is spin
taken as written
CE is the Church of England, the established church
a con is a convict, a criminal
a sort is a class or kind

explanation.surface: Royal public relations meets crooks and class.
explanation.definitionFit: The husband of a reigning queen holds this title, most famously Albert, so he is a royal.
